answer.reason: North Dakota is a small labor market (total covered private employment roughly 350,000-400,000), and its QCEW data has historically shown NAICS 54 Professional, scientific, and technical services at roughly 17,000-18,000 private jobs—well below national-average industry shares, since North Dakota's economy is weighted toward mining/oil & gas, agriculture, construction, transportation, and government. A December 2024 level of about 17,068 covered jobs is consistent with this sector's established size in the state, whereas 27,174 would be far above any previously reported level for NAICS 54 in North Dakota (and more plausibly corresponds to a different industry or a larger state). Since the cited QCEW CSV could not be directly queried here, this determination rests on prior knowledge of North Dakota QCEW industry levels rather than the file itself.
